chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Ju'ni, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Imamate will not gather in two brothers after Hasan and Husayn (peace be upon them). It is only in the descendants, and the descendants of the descendants.
ai.seo_question: What is the rule regarding the Imamate in brothers after Hasan and Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from Kitab al-Ghayba establishes the principle of 'franchise exclusion' (jam' al-imama fi akhawayn), clarifying that while the Imamate may pass between brothers in specific instances, it generally follows a single direct male lineage (awqab) after the era of Hasan and Husayn. This ruling was crucial for Shia jurists to resolve succession disputes, particularly during the Minor and Major Ghaibat, by affirming the continuity of a singular, undisputed Imam rather than co-ruling siblings.
